findings.title: Tenant-owned tables exist without RLS: an interim, documented exception to security invariant 1 that GOZ-0003 must close
evidence: src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/Migrations/20261116000000_Organizations.cs creates organizations, invitations and memberships with no ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and no policy
src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/GozlemeDbContext.cs:71-72 comment: tenant keys exist so that GOZ-0003 can enable RLS
docs/architecture/security-invariants.md invariant 1: every tenant-owned row is protected by application authorization AND effective PostgreSQL RLS
docs/specs/002-organizations/plan.md Complexity Tracking records the violation, justified by roadmap order (GOZ-0000-IF-03); spec.md Assumptions: 'This spec does not claim RLS protection'
docs/engineering/local-development.md:69 states isolation is application-layer only until GOZ-0003
gozleme_app has DML on the tables through the foundation default privileges (data-model.md header)
findings.recommendation: Maintainer explicitly acknowledges the interim invariant-1 exception at GOZ-0002 PR review, and confirms that GOZ-0003 runs before any other spec that adds tenant-owned data and that no release or tag is cut while the exception is open. GOZ-0003 enables RLS on all three tables and adds them to its catalog test. GOZ-0039's release gate verifies effective RLS on every tenant-owned table. No spec may claim RLS protection before GOZ-0003 merges.
findings.disposition: human-decision: acknowledge the interim invariant-1 exception and its closure conditions; downstream prompt obligations already applied (GOZ-0003, GOZ-0039 and the cross-cutting section in all future prompts)

findings.title: The implementation depends on access paths that cross tenants before any tenant is known; a naive per-tenant RLS policy would break them or tempt trust in caller-set settings
evidence: src/Gozleme.Api/Organizations/OrganizationEndpoints.cs:51-70 ListAsync reads every memberships row of the account and joins organizations
src/Gozleme.Api/Organizations/OrganizationAccess.cs:17-25 FindMembershipAsync is the check that establishes the tenant; it reads memberships by (organization_id, user_id)
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:296 redemption finds invitations by code_hash FOR UPDATE before the organization is known, then inserts a membership (:312-320)
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:72-92 creation inserts the organization and its first membership in one SaveChanges
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:173 removal locks the organizations row FOR UPDATE
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:151-155 the member list joins the global users table for emails
src/Gozleme.Api/Identity/OperatorCommands.cs:122-150 seed resets the Seeded Demo Org as gozleme_app with no HTTP request (R3-19 operator/tenant separation)
findings.recommendation: GOZ-0003 designs RLS that keeps these paths working: an account-scoped visibility rule on memberships as well as the tenant rule; a redemption path where possession of the 160-bit code is the proof; creation inserting a new tenant; and a defined operator context for seed. The account identity used by RLS comes from the authenticated principal, set by the application in the same transaction. Tests prove that a forged or stale setting cannot read another account's memberships or invitations.

findings.title: The interim role-neutral rule must be replaced by GOZ-0004 roles; the initial-role migration for existing organizations needs a maintainer decision during GOZ-0004
evidence: docs/specs/002-organizations/spec.md FR-015, FR-016, FR-018; progress.yaml decision member-powers ('GOZ-0004 restricts with roles')
OrganizationEndpoints.cs: every organization-scoped handler calls OrganizationAccess.FindMembershipAsync first, and any membership row grants every action
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:173,190 the last-member guard runs under the organizations row lock
contracts/organizations-api.openapi.yaml:52 the error enum already includes 'forbidden', which is unused
OrganizationTelemetry.cs:43-51 failure categories have no 'forbidden'

tests/Gozleme.Api.IntegrationTests/OrganizationBoundaryTests.cs Extra_privilege_fields_are_ignored_and_the_creator_has_no_special_standing: the creator can be removed, and joined_via and created_by grant nothing
findings.recommendation: GOZ-0004 keeps the membership check first, so non-members still get identical 404s. It adds the permission check after it, which may answer 403 forbidden to members. It turns the last-member guard into a guard that always keeps at least one member able to manage membership, under the same row lock, and it adds a bounded 'forbidden' telemetry category. The rule that gives existing members their initial roles is chosen with the maintainer during GOZ-0004 clarification, never inferred.
findings.disposition: applied-to-future-prompts (the initial-role migration rule is routed to the maintainer in GOZ-0004 clarification)

findings.title: Removing a member does not revoke the open invitations that member created, so a removed account can rejoin with a code it minted earlier
evidence: OrganizationEndpoints.cs:158-210 RemoveMemberAsync deletes only the memberships row and does not touch invitations
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:296-320 redemption accepts any open code for a non-member, including the account that created it
spec.md FR-017 requires removal to take effect on the next request, which it does; US3-5 allows rejoining with a new valid invitation; no requirement covers the removed member's own outstanding codes
Mitigation today: any remaining member sees open invitations with their creator (FR-012) and can revoke them manually
No test covers this case (MembershipTests.cs, InvitationTests.cs)
findings.recommendation: Preferred: a bounded GOZ-0002 correction. Remove and leave revoke, in the same transaction, the open invitations created by the departing account. Set revoked_by to the actor and emit audit 1104 for each one. Add an integration test showing a removed member cannot rejoin with its own earlier code. Alternative: accept this as an interim residual that GOZ-0004 must close; the GOZ-0004 prompt already carries the obligation either way.
findings.disposition: human-decision: fix now in GOZ-0002 (recommended) or defer to GOZ-0004; GOZ-0004 prompt obligation applied

findings.title: Organization-scoped API, page and existence-hiding conventions that every later tenant-data spec must follow
evidence: OrganizationEndpoints.cs:22-43 routes under /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}; the ID is a string with no route constraint (research R3)
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:24,45-49 NoStore filter; an empty 404 for malformed, unknown and non-member IDs (OrganizationIsolationTests.Non_member_unknown_and_malformed_ids_get_identical_empty_404s)
research.md R4: activeOrganizationId is computed from memberships.selected_at and is never authority
web/src/lib/organizations.ts:44 segment() neutralises dot segments; web/src/app/organizations/[organizationId]/not-found.tsx
docs/prompts/*: no future prompt stated these conventions
findings.recommendation: Organization-scoped endpoints take the organization ID in the path and never from an implicit active organization. They check membership first, through FindMembershipAsync or its GOZ-0003/GOZ-0004 successor, and answer identical empty 404s with no-store. Pages live under /organizations/[organizationId]/ and use segment(). New tenant-owned tables carry organization_id with a foreign key to organizations(id).

data-model.md: memberships rows are deleted on removal; invitations are kept after use, revocation or expiry; there is no organization deletion or lifecycle (R3-24 post-MVP)

findings.recommendation: GOZ-0035 adds memberships, invitations and co-member email exposure to the retention inventory, and defines erasure behaviour for the last member before any account erasure exists. GOZ-0039 round-trips the three tables in backup and restore and documents that a restore brings back removed memberships. GOZ-0014 does not assume organizations can be deleted.
